Senses.PreferredTarget: ten thousand strings of cash around the waist
AlternateTargets: wearing ten thousand strings of cash
SearchAliases: ten thousand cash at the waist
wealth and a crane to Yangzhou

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Ten thousand strings of cash around the waist supplies the wealth in the comic wish to be rich, immortal, and immediately in Yangzhou: the next line rides there on a crane. Chan masters preserve the complete impossible combination as a verse ending, an answer, and a criticism of wanting every incompatible advantage at once.
EvidenceBody: Tangzhong Zhongren caps his imperial verse with the money-and-crane couplet.
Dahui Zonggao adds the couplet to his comment on Juzhi’s finger.
Yun’e Xi answers a question about the Buddha’s star-sighting with the same Yangzhou wish.
Juelang Daosheng quotes the story king’s conditional promise that everyone may ride to Yangzhou.
Tianran Hanshi invokes the saying in a letter against refusing to relinquish anything while hoping to gain everything.

Senses.Note: Seventy-seven exact hits occur in fifty-one frozen works; five distinct deployments retain the full Yangzhou setting rather than isolating the money clause.
